title: Split Into k Groups of Equal Sum

concept.title: Put each number in a bucket, and never try two buckets that look the same
body: Split `n` numbers into `k` groups with the same sum. The sum of every group must be `total / k`, so first check that `total` is divisible by `k` and that no number is larger than the target. Then place the numbers one by one into `k` buckets; a number may go to a bucket only if the bucket sum stays at most the target.

Two pruning ideas make this fast enough: place the **big numbers first** (they have few possible buckets, so mistakes show early), and **never try two buckets with the same current sum** for the same number, because they are interchangeable. Without the second rule the search would try all `k!` ways to name the buckets of every partial solution.

statement: Given `n` positive integers and a number `k`, decide whether the integers can be split into `k` groups (every integer goes to exactly one group) so that all `k` groups have exactly the same sum. Print `yes` or `no`.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: The total is 20, so each group has 5: {5}, {1, 4}, {2, 3}, {2, 3}.

hints: The groups must have the sum total / k: if it is not an integer, the answer is no.
Sort in decreasing order and place the numbers into buckets one by one.
For a number, skip a bucket whose sum equals the sum of a bucket already tried.

explanation: After the divisibility checks, the numbers are placed from the largest to the smallest into `k` buckets with the target as the limit; a bucket whose current sum was already tried for this number is skipped. All numbers placed means all buckets are exactly full.
solution.complexity: Time exponential in the worst case but small with the pruning, space O(n).
